Mixed Measures **__VERSION__** — a local-first desktop workspace for mixed-methods research: qualitative and quantitative data in one project, with shared participants, codes, and memos. Everything stays on your own computer — no account, no uploads, no telemetry.

**What's new in this release**

This release is about three things: working with colleagues on copies of a project —
a copy can now be merged back, a coder is recognised as a person rather than by name,
and someone who withdrew stays withdrawn; numbers that were wrong, most of them in
grouped charts and the exported R script; and imports that keep every word of your
documents.

- 🔴 **Grouped figures showed the wrong group's numbers — check any you reported.** A Canvas bar chart, table or histogram of a grouped variable (a mean score by site, say) showed one number, and it belonged to the records with no value for the grouping variable. The Analysis view's Summary Table and Histogram did the same under *Group by*, and the Word export's table was wrong for every grouped chart. Each group now shows its own value and n.
- 🔴 **Bar chart labels could show another bar's value.** In the frequency, horizontal and stacked bar charts, every label after an empty category showed an earlier bar's value, while the bars themselves were right. A grouped vertical bar chart of answers also left out answers only other groups gave, and a group whose answers were all missing data was drawn as 0%. **A chart image saved, or a Canvas exported, before this release may carry wrong labels — redraw it to check.**
- 🔴 **A scale measured in several datasets scores its respondents again.** A record was judged against every item of the group in every dataset, so a record could lose its score over one skipped item — and in three complete datasets no record was scored at all — and a saved t-test or ANOVA on such a score failed or used too few people. Scores and saved tests the new rule changes are marked out of date.
- 🔴 **The exported R script gives the app's numbers and runs to the end.** It replaced your computed variables with R's own, different results; could stop at a long, non-Latin or reserved name; read an answer spelled "NA" as missing and turned text answers into numbers; and counted a proportion saved with "=" differently from the app. **It could also run R code that arrived in someone else's project file or codebook; it no longer can.** A few column names in the exported data file change, and categorical and demographic variables (age, say) now arrive in R as text — the changelog lists both.
- 🔴 **A formula that compares a variable with a quoted answer now works.** On a variable with value labels, `[Q1] == "Agree"` was false on every row, without a warning. Computed variables written this way are marked out of date when you update; *Recompute* brings them up to date, and marks what is built on them out of date in turn.
- 🔴 **Imported documents keep every word.** Text between `<` and `>` was deleted from text, Word and PDF imports, and Word imports dropped the text in tracked changes, form fields, smart tags and text boxes. Tracked changes are now imported as if accepted, and the import counts what it still leaves out — tables, comments, footnotes, and headers and footers among them. **A document imported before this release may be missing text; importing the original file again brings it back.**
- **A colleague's copy can now be merged back, and a coder is recognised as a person.** *Import* now keeps a project's identity, so the copy a colleague codes can come back to you through *Merge coding in…*; it first asks which of the file's people is you. Each coder carries an identity in the project file, so two people who are both called "Researcher" stay two coders. Copies imported before this release cannot be merged back: export the project again from this version.
- **Someone who withdrew stays withdrawn, and their words go where the app had copied them.** A merged or split turn holding their words is blanked; Canvas quotes, the Audit Trail and saved results no longer keep them, with one exception the changelog names; and merging an older copy, importing one or linking records does not bring them back. The confirmation now says what is removed — your notes and codes on their survey answers included — and no open page goes on showing their data. A withdrawal made in a colleague's copy does not reach your project through a merge: withdraw the person in your own project as well.
- **Editing a turn keeps its quotes on their words.** Fixing a typo used to shift every later quote on that turn onto different words. A quote now follows its words, and when an edit changes the words at a quote's edge, the workbench shows the quote before and after and asks.
- **Updates are safer.** If updating your data fails, everything is undone and your previous version can still open it; a large project from an early version finishes updating instead of timing out; and from this version on, data a newer version has updated is refused with a message instead of being copied at every launch.
- **Security.** The desktop app moves to Electron 44.9.3, which blocks compromised certificates someone intercepting your network could have used to impersonate the update check. Canvas HTML and PDF exports escape every value and carry their own content-security policy, and a group label starting with "=" reaches Excel as text, never as a formula.
- **And a round of smaller fixes.** A canvas with a quote waiting in Unsorted opens again, and Descriptives charts can be placed on the Canvas again. A statistic that could not be computed shows "—" instead of zero. Coding and ratings refresh the figures they feed, and the Ratings page keeps your place. A damaged Word file is refused with an explanation, and failure messages no longer send you to a server log. The Kruskal–Wallis effect size is now the ε² it is labelled as; values move up, most on small samples. One control character no longer stops an Excel, Word or codebook export. Scatter plots show their points in dark mode, and the Data view's page buttons keep keyboard focus.

<!-- Update the next paragraph at every cut: the cut-off is the last release that used the PREVIOUS .mmproject format, not a fixed number. 1.5.4 introduced format 7; 1.5.5, 1.5.6, 1.5.7 and 1.5.8 write the same format. 1.5.8 adds coder identities and the withdrawal record to it, which older versions ignore. -->
- 🔴 **Read this before you share a project file.** **Project files saved by __VERSION__ do not open in 1.5.3 or earlier** — 1.5.4 changed how a project file stores your data, and an older version refuses such a file and says so rather than importing a project that appears to be empty. **Files from older versions still open here as normal.** 1.5.4 and later write the same format, **but versions before 1.5.8 ignore what 1.5.8 adds to a project file — who each coder is, and what a withdrawal removed — and leave both out of anything they export.** If you are working with a colleague, update together before you exchange `.mmproject` files, above all for a project from which someone has withdrawn. **Backups (`.mmbackup`) are not affected.**
- **If your team shared a project before 1.5.8, the first merge after updating may ask about people you already work with.** Each computer gave its coders an identity of its own when it updated, so Merge's *Confirm coders* step can know a colleague here only by name, and waits for your answer. Choose *Map to* their name only for the same person, and *Add as new coder* for anyone else: a wrong answer makes two people one coder, or one person two. This version does not yet remember a *Map to* answer, so the question comes back at each merge of that colleague's copy.
- 🔴 **This update changes your database, and takes a copy first.** Whichever version you are coming from, the first launch updates your database: every coder is given an identity, a place is made for the record of what a withdrawal removed, and formulas that compare a variable with a quoted answer are marked out of date. The startup screen says it is updating your data; keep Mixed Measures open until it finishes — a large project can take several minutes. If the update fails, it is undone completely and your previous version can still open the data. **Once __VERSION__ has updated your data, do not go back to an earlier version:** 1.5.7 and earlier cannot open it, and each attempt replaces one of the copies taken before the update, until none from before it is left. If something goes wrong, install __VERSION__ again. **If your project matters to you, copy your data folder somewhere of your own before upgrading:** a copy you control is the only one the app's own rotation can never reach. Full details in the [changelog](https://github.com/__REPO__/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md).

## Which file should I download?

Pick the one for your computer and click it:

- **macOS** (Apple Silicon — M1 or later) → **[MixedMeasures-__VERSION__-mac-arm64.dmg](https://github.com/__REPO__/releases/download/v__VERSION__/MixedMeasures-__VERSION__-mac-arm64.dmg)**
- **Windows** → **[MixedMeasures-__VERSION__-win-x64.exe](https://github.com/__REPO__/releases/download/v__VERSION__/MixedMeasures-__VERSION__-win-x64.exe)**
- **Linux** → **[MixedMeasures-__VERSION__-linux-x86_64.AppImage](https://github.com/__REPO__/releases/download/v__VERSION__/MixedMeasures-__VERSION__-linux-x86_64.AppImage)**

> **Not sure if your Mac is Apple Silicon?** Click the Apple menu (top-left) → **About This Mac**. If the **Chip** line says "Apple M1" (or any later Apple chip), this is the right file. Older Intel Macs aren't supported in this release.

<!-- Requirements: re-check at every cut. macOS from electron/package.json build.mac.minimumSystemVersion (the release's "macOS floor" step proves it against every binary); Windows from Electron's own README "Platform support"; Linux from the AppImage's highest GLIBC_ symbol version (2.38 measured on v1.5.5 — the frozen backend's libraries, collected on the ubuntu-24.04 runner). -->
**What it runs on**

- **macOS 14 (Sonoma) or later**, on Apple Silicon. A Mac on an older version is not offered this update; every Apple Silicon Mac can be updated to macOS 14.
- **Windows 10 or 11**, 64-bit.
- **Linux**, 64-bit, with glibc 2.38 or newer — Ubuntu 24.04 or later, for example.

You can **ignore the other files** in the Assets list below (the `.blockmap` and `.yml` files) — the app uses those for updates; you don't need to download them.

## First launch

The installers are signed (and notarized on macOS), so the verified publisher is **George Chavez**. Because the app is new and independent, your system may show a one-time prompt the first time you open it. This is normal and fades as more people install it — it is not a sign that anything is wrong.

- **macOS:** drag Mixed Measures to your Applications folder. If it doesn't open on a double-click, right-click it → **Open**.
- **Windows:** if you see "Windows protected your PC," click **More info → Run anyway** (you'll see *George Chavez* listed as the publisher).

See the [README](https://github.com/__REPO__#readme) to get started.
